enforcement_authorities: European Commission (coordinating joint actions, EU funding programmes, AI Watch monitoring, and companion legislative proposals)
EU Member States and national competent authorities / notified bodies (national AI strategies, RRF investment plans, and planned ex-ante/ex-post AI Act compliance oversight)
EU specialised agencies and bodies (ENISA, Joint Research Centre / AI Watch, Eurostat, Europol, Frontex, eu-LISA, EASA)
compliance_deadlines: 2021–2027: Multiannual funding cycle targeting at least EUR 1 billion/year from Horizon Europe and Digital Europe to leverage EUR 20 billion/year in total EU public and private AI investment, alongside up to EUR 134 billion RRF digital expenditure target

2021 (Q2–Q4): Launch European Alliances on industrial data/edge/cloud and microelectronics, co-programmed AI/Data/Robotics PPP, first TEF/EDIH/data-space calls, Adopt AI programme, horizontal AI Act legislative proposal (COM(2021) 206), European Health Data Space proposal (Q4 2021), and mobility AI roadmap

2022: Commission proposals to adapt EU liability framework and sectoral safety legislation, launch of mandatory Horizon Europe gender-equality-plan eligibility criterion, TEF deployments in health/robotics/smart communities, vehicle automation/cybersecurity rules applicable from July 6, 2022, and Commission timeline/methodology for the next Coordinated Plan review

2023–2025: Completion of Destination Earth Phase 1 (end 2023), common European agriculture data space and Agriculture of Data PPP (2023–2024), and EU-wide European Health Data Space infrastructure (by 2025)
penalties_summary: As a non-binding strategic coordination plan (COM(2021) 205 final ANNEX) accompanying the Commission's April 2021 AI Act proposal, the 2021 Review imposes no direct civil or criminal penalties. Compliance relies on Member State coordination, Horizon Europe and Digital Europe funding eligibility rules (such as ethics-by-design and mandatory gender equality plans from 2022), public procurement contract criteria (such as Fair AI minimal capabilities and prospective environmental scoring), voluntary codes of conduct, and capacity-building for the separate horizontal AI regulation's planned ex-ante conformity assessment and ex-post market surveillance system.
implementation_notes: Published April 21, 2021 as the Annex to COM(2021) 205 final alongside the initial EU AI Act legislative proposal (COM(2021) 206), updating the 2018 Coordinated Plan across 4 strategic pillars and 17 chapters (7 horizontal + 7 high-impact sectoral areas: climate/environment, health, robotics, public sector, law enforcement/migration/asylum, mobility, and agriculture), plus a 40-action 2021–2025+ timeline (Appendix 1) and Member State strategy/budget inventory (Appendix 2). Mobilises Digital Europe, Horizon Europe, InvestEU, and the Recovery and Resilience Facility to scale European data spaces, EuroHPC supercomputing, low-power edge/neuromorphic chips, AI Lighthouse research networks, 210 European Digital Innovation Hubs, Testing and Experimentation Facilities, regulatory sandboxes, AI-on-demand marketplace, and trustworthy public procurement. Retained as a superseded 2021 historical baseline for longitudinal EU policy-framing analysis.
